newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends marginally down at 10.20-10.75 pct.
newsitem.headline: India call ends marginally down at 10.20-10.75 pct.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday in the 10.20-10.70 range, marginally down from the day's opening quotes of 10.50-10.75 percent, dealers said.
Most of the day's trade was in the 10.5-10.6 percent range, they said.
In dull secondary market trade, prices of government securities were little changed from Wednesday's levels, they said.
Trades were reported in the 12 percent 1999 government of India stock at a yield of 13.90 percent against Wednesday's 13.89 percent, they said.
The 13.82 percent 2002 stock was traded at 13.91 percent against 13.93. Buying interest pushed down yields on the zero-coupon bond 1999 to 14.09 percent from 14.16 percent, dealers said.
The treasury bill maturing on September 30 was traded on Thursday at 10.6 percent against Wednesday's 10.25 percent.
Dealers said the commercial paper market was inactive.
In certificates of deposit (CDs), a secondary market trade was reported in a CD maturing in January 1997 at a yield of 14.30 percent, dealers said.
Rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 17.0-19.0 percent range with few deals reported.
